name: Conductex-44
description: Conductex-44 is a metallic-phase single-wall CNT yarn produced by Apex Nanofabrication, optimized for electrical conductivity rather than structural strength. Individual tubes are sorted by chirality during fabrication to select only those with near-zero bandgap — the resulting yarn carries current with resistivity lower than copper at one-hundredth the weight, and can be woven, braided, or printed into complex three-dimensional circuit geometries. It is the backbone material of flexible electronics, wearable computing, and high-frequency signal transmission in cyberware.
story_hooks: Conductex-44 is so efficient at carrying high-frequency signals that black-market fabricators use it to build undetectable communication relays hidden inside everyday garments.
A cyberware malfunction trace leads back to a substituted Conductex-44 component — someone swapped genuine material for a conductive polymer knockoff inside a medical-grade neural implant.

Apex Nanofabrication's chirality-sorting line requires a proprietary catalyst that comes from a single offworld source; when that supply is disrupted, every Conductex-44-dependent manufacturer scrambles.
